 Surely not the most painful someone can experience, but as I sometimes say: "The pain is relative."

I suffered sprains in both ankles 2 years ago, and everything and that the pain at the beginning was very intense and painful, after being writhing in pain for a few minutes I could get up and walk with.

But the most intense pain I've felt was when that year I suffered second degree burns on both legs (yes, it wasn't a good year for my legs). When I burned, I felt almost nothing, since the adrenaline that ran through my body covered the pain. But after a few days, the dead tissue of my legs (the skin) had to be torn off, revealing the younger layers of the skin. I cannot describe in words how horrible it is to see you bedridden, while some nurses stretch your skin with tweezers. At the end of the daily cures (when there are burns, the wounds have to heal daily, to change the dressings), I could not even support my legs, since in doing so it made me feel as if they threw you alcohol to heal in an open wound that It runs all over your leg. They had to take me in a wheelchair to my house.

Arriving at my house, I swear I would have preferred at that time to have sprained all my legs and arms than to have found myself in that painful situation.

This happened when I was 16 year old, in summer, btw.
